text:
sachin: Heads up — CI microbench alert for kv_warmup after merging feature/optimizer-queue. perf-bot flagged a +12% median latency delta on the azure-x86-rt runner. PR: https://git/repo/pull/12531

perf-bot: [AUTOMATED] Benchmark threshold exceeded
- bench: kv_warmup_microbench
- baseline commit: abcdef1..
- head commit: 1234567
- median latency: baseline=9.4ms head=10.55ms (+12.3%)
- kv_hit_rate: baseline=0.74 head=0.62
- artifact: https://ci/artifacts/12531/bench/html

jon: ack. does the profiler show more kernel switches or batch-size skew? any traces from the failing runner?

maria: I pulled the artifact — the trace shows a notable increase in kernel_selector choosing matmul_fused_v2 for short sequences (~64-256). That kernel has a slightly higher setup cost and seems to interact poorly with our kv-prefetch path.

eileen: quick snippet from the runner logs: 
```
[2026-03-18T15:02:11Z] Selected kernel: matmul_fused_v2 (prefetch=true)
[2026-03-18T15:02:11Z] kv_cache: hit_rate=0.62 evictions=48
[2026-03-18T15:02:11Z] batch_size_distribution: 1:40% 2:35% 4:25%
```

jon: can we reproduce locally? I'll kick off a targeted microbench on perf-rt-02 with the head commit. Suggest: 
```
git checkout 1234567 && ./tools/run_microbench.sh --bench kv_warmup --seqlens 64,128,256 --warmup 50 --samples 200
```

sachin: @jon when you run, capture kernel selector dumps (export DEBUG_KERNEL_SELECTOR=1). Also run with KV_STATS=1 so we can see per-run hitrates.

jon: ran the command on perf-rt-02, reproduced: head +13% median vs baseline. KV hit dropped from 0.75->0.61 locally. Kernel dump shows ~72% matmul_fused_v2 on seqlen 128.

maria: interesting — matmul_fused_v2 was added in the optimizer-queue change to improve throughput for long sequences. Looks like our selection heuristic didn't constrain by kv-warmup cost.

eileen: minimal repro suggests the regression is selection heuristic only, not batcher. I think a targeted revert/hotfix to adjust kernel selector weighting should fix it.

jon: propose a quick revert of the heuristic tweak in commit abcdef1 (or add a guard: if kv_hit_rate < 0.7 prefer matmul_v1). Which is faster to ship?

maria: guard is safer and should be small — I'll open a PR with the guard and a unit test for kv-warmup path. If that lands we can roll forward.

ci-bot: @maria opened PR #12545: "kernel-selector: prefer stable kernel when kv hit low" — running microbench CI.

perf-bot: [AUTOMATED] Microbench run queued for PR #12545. Baseline comparison will be reported in-thread when complete.

jon: for the rollout plan: if PR #12545 fails to bring <5% diff, revert commit abcdef1 from main and cherry-pick later. I'm taking oncall for the revert.

sachin: thanks. please also add a golden test that exercises kv warmup sequences so this doesn't slip.

perf-bot: [AUTOMATED] PR #12545 microbench results: kv_warmup delta = +1.2% (within threshold).

maria: landed and merged. Monitoring CI now.

jon: rolled forward on main. Current CI on azure-x86-rt shows green for microbench suite.

eileen: leaving a note on the changelog: optimizer-queue kernel-selector change required kv-aware guard; created follow-up issue #1729 to revisit matmul_fused_v2 heuristics for mixed-warmup workloads. :memo:

sachin: excellent work. closing the alert. Will follow up on the longer-term work in #1729.
